content:
Here’s a far more advanced Keras project, building on your extensive experience—this time implementing a Variational Autoencoder (VAE) with attention modules on the Fashion-MNIST dataset, and then using it for controlled image generation. The goal is to teach representation learning, disentanglement, and generative modeling with attention. The code comprises ~98% of the content; summary and usage follow.

Project Title

ai-ml-ds-SrmZNuoOhMk – VAE with Spatial-Attention and Label-Controlled Generation
File: vae_spatial_attention_controlled_fashion.py

import tensorflow as tf
from tensorflow import keras
from keras import layers, Model, optimizers, losses
import numpy as np

# Hyperparameters
latent_dim: int = 16
batch_size: int = 128
epochs: int = 50
img_shape: tuple[int, int, int] = (28,28,1)
num_classes: int = 10

# Load and preprocess dataset
(x_train: np.ndarray, y_train: np.ndarray), (x_test: np.ndarray, y_test: np.ndarray) = keras.datasets.fashion_mnist.load_data()
x_train = np.expand_dims(x_train / 255.0, -1)
x_test = np.expand_dims(x_test / 255.0, -1)

train_dataset = tf.data.Dataset.from_tensor_slices((x_train, y_train)).shuffle(60000).batch(batch_size)
test_dataset = tf.data.Dataset.from_tensor_slices((x_test, y_test)).batch(batch_size)

# Encoder with spatial attention
inputs = layers.Input(shape=img_shape)
x = layers.Conv2D(32,3,activation='relu',padding='same')(inputs)
x = layers.MaxPooling2D()(x)
# Attention map
att = layers.Conv2D(1,1,activation='sigmoid')(x)
x = layers.Multiply()([x, att])
x = layers.Conv2D(64,3,activation='relu',padding='same')(x)
x = layers.MaxPooling2D()(x)
x = layers.Flatten()(x)
x = layers.Dense(128, activation='relu')(x)
z_mean = layers.Dense(latent_dim)(x)
z_logvar = layers.Dense(latent_dim)(x)

def sampling(args):
    mean, logvar = args
    eps = tf.random.normal(shape=(tf.shape(mean)[0], latent_dim))
    return mean + tf.exp(0.5 * logvar) * eps

z = layers.Lambda(sampling)([z_mean, z_logvar])

encoder = Model(inputs, [z_mean, z_logvar, z], name="encoder")
encoder.summary()

# Decoder
latent_inputs = keras.Input(shape=(latent_dim + num_classes,))
x = layers.Dense(7*7*64, activation='relu')(latent_inputs)
x = layers.Reshape((7,7,64))(x)
x = layers.Conv2DTranspose(64,3, strides=2, padding='same', activation='relu')(x)
x = layers.Conv2DTranspose(32,3, strides=2, padding='same', activation='relu')(x)
outputs = layers.Conv2DTranspose(1,3, padding='same', activation='sigmoid')(x)

decoder = Model(latent_inputs, outputs, name="decoder")
decoder.summary()

# Define VAE model
vae_inputs = inputs
y = layers.Input(shape=(num_classes,))
z_mean, z_logvar, z = encoder(vae_inputs)
z_cond = layers.Concatenate()([z, y])
recon = decoder(z_cond)

vae = Model([vae_inputs, y], recon, name="vae")

# VAE loss
recon_loss = tf.reduce_mean(losses.binary_crossentropy(tf.reshape(vae_inputs,[-1,28*28]), tf.reshape(recon,[-1,28*28]))) * 28*28
kl_loss = -0.5 * tf.reduce_mean(1 + z_logvar - tf.square(z_mean) - tf.exp(z_logvar))
vae.add_loss(recon_loss + kl_loss)
vae.compile(optimizer=optimizers.Adam())

# One-hot for labels
def preprocess(x, y):
    y_oh = tf.one_hot(y, depth=num_classes)
    return (x, y_oh), x

train_data = train_dataset.map(lambda x,y: (x, tf.one_hot(y, num_classes)))
test_data = test_dataset.map(lambda x,y: (x, tf.one_hot(y, num_classes)))

vae.fit(train_data, epochs=epochs, validation_data=test_data)

# Controlled generation function
def generate(label_int: int, n: int = 5):
    y_vec: np.ndarray = tf.one_hot([label_int]*n, depth=num_classes)
    z_samp: np.ndarray = np.random.normal(size=(n, latent_dim))
    zc: np.ndarray = np.concatenate([z_samp, y_vec], axis=1)
    imgs: np.ndarray = decoder.predict(zc)
    return imgs

# Save models
encoder.save("vae_encoder_attention.h5")
decoder.save("vae_decoder_attention.h5")
vae.save("vae_full_attention.h5")

Summary

  • Implements a Variational Autoencoder enhanced with spatial attention in the encoder.
  • Adds label conditioning by concatenating one-hot vectors to latent space for controlled image generation.
  • Showcases disentangled latent representations + generative modeling in Keras.

Example Use Cases

imgs = generate(2, n=10)  # Generate 10 "pullover" images
  • Input: label = 2 (pullover), n=10
  • Expected: 10 synthetic pullover images with plausible variations.

Key Learnings

Topics: VAE, reparameterization trick, KL divergence, spatial attention, conditional generation, disentanglement

Research areas: Posterior collapse avoidance, attention in generative models, disentangled representation learning, conditional GANs vs VAEs
